summary: A user ran curl to download from localhost to /dev/null
likely_cause: User executing a curl command to download data from localhost without saving it, possibly for testing or debugging
recommended_action: Check user activity and verify if the command was intentional; monitor for further suspicious activity

summary: Root user modified the root's bash history file in /tmp
likely_cause: Normal admin activity or potential malicious activity modifying shell history
recommended_action: Check for recent shell commands in /root/.bash_history and verify user activity

summary: A user executed curl to download a file from an external HTTP server at port 8099 using /tmp as working directory.
likely_cause: User running a tool to interact with an external service (e.g., AWS IoT Core) without proper authorization or context.
recommended_action: Verify user permissions for accessing port 8099 and check if the external server is authorized; investigate if this is part of legitimate admin work or a potential breach.

summary: A user ran curl to download from localhost to /dev/null in /tmp directory
likely_cause: User executing a local curl command to download data from localhost without saving it
recommended_action: Check if the user has legitimate need for this command and verify if it was part of normal admin tasks

summary: A user's bash history file was modified in /home/<NAME>/
likely_cause: User activity (bash shell) modifying their own history file
recommended_action: Check if the history file was modified by a legitimate user or if it's part of a malicious session

summary: A file named test-ai in /etc/cron.d was deleted by the system monitoring tool ossec.
likely_cause: The ossec security tool detected a file deletion event in the cron configuration directory, which is a normal part of its monitoring activity.
recommended_action: Verify the integrity of the cron.d directory and check for any unauthorized changes in the ossec configuration.

alert: UFW: possible port scan - multiple blocked connections from the same source.
summary: UFW blocked multiple connection attempts from an external source attempting to scan port 8080
likely_cause: Reconnaissance activity by an attacker probing for open ports
recommended_action: Review firewall logs for additional scan attempts and check if port 8080 is intentionally open for services

summary: A user's bash history file was modified by a shell session running as the user.
likely_cause: Normal user activity modifying their own shell history, as the audit logs show the user (UID 1000) ran bash in a terminal session (pts0) and modified their .bash_history file.
recommended_action: Verify the user's shell history for unusual commands and check if the user has legitimate reasons for modifying their history file.

alert: Listened ports status (netstat) changed (new port opened or closed).
summary: New port 4444 opened on the system, which is not a standard port for SSH or DNS services.
likely_cause: Potential unauthorized service or malicious activity opening port 4444, as it is a known port for remote code execution and exploitation.
recommended_action: Immediately investigate the source of the port 4444, check for unauthorized processes, and block the port if confirmed malicious.

alert: Listened ports status (netstat) changed (new port opened or closed).
summary: Netstat shows new SSH (port 22) and DNS (port 53) services running with init and systemd-resolve processes
likely_cause: Normal system services starting up or configuration changes
recommended_action: Verify that SSH and DNS services are expected to be running on this system and check for any recent configuration changes

alert: New group added to the system.
summary: A new group named demo-user with GID 1002 was created on the system.
likely_cause: An administrator or user running useradd command to create a new group for system management.
recommended_action: Verify the purpose of the new group and ensure it aligns with organizational policies; check if the group is being used by legitimate users or services.

alert: New user added to the system.
summary: A new user account was created with UID 1002, GID 1002, home directory /home/<NAME>, and shell /bin/sh via the adduser command from a terminal session.
likely_cause: A legitimate system administrator adding a new user account for normal operations, as the user is created with standard permissions and the command originates from a terminal session (from=/dev/pts/0).
recommended_action: Verify the user's purpose and permissions by checking the user's home directory and shell configuration; ensure the user is part of the expected groups (syslog, adduser) and that the account is not a security risk.
